investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GETs (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser) of the venue's own calendar page and one real event's own detail page. The calendar page is Angular Universal server-side-rendered: its retained response already contains (a) a <script id="serverApp-state" type="application/json"> transfer-state blob whose events-by-month query results give each event's own Firebase-style id and a genuine UTC 'start' ISO timestamp, and (b) fully server-rendered DOM spans (title/subtitle/location/category/local date parts) for the same events, matched by a shared data-id/id key — all read directly from the raw HTTP response text, no JS execution needed. This platform's custom '&q;' in-script escaping (used in place of '"') was mechanically reversed with a plain string replace before JSON-parsing; the resulting JSON parsed cleanly. The event's own detail page additionally carries a clean, standard schema.org JSON-LD 'Event' block with the same UTC startDate plus location/name.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.kesselhaus.net/en/calendar already exposed, in one retained HTTP response, both a server-rendered DOM (title/date/location/category per event card) and an embedded Angular Universal transfer-state JSON blob giving each event's own id and a genuine UTC startDate, joinable by a shared key. A second plain curl GET of one real event's own detail page additionally confirmed a clean, standard schema.org JSON-LD Event block for that same event. No client-side JS execution or browser was needed at any point — this directly answers the investigation question at Level 1.

venue_reference: Kesselhaus / Kulturbrauerei (concert venue within the Kulturbrauerei complex, Prenzlauer Berg, Berlin — Knaackstraße 97, 10435 Berlin)

identity.notes: The venue's own dedicated first-party domain, kesselhaus.net, self-identifies directly: its retained homepage <title> is 'Kesselhaus | Festivals, Konzerte, Theater, Lesungen, Tanz, Partys und Clubreihen in Berlin', and its own retained 'EventVenue' JSON-LD block on the calendar page states 'name':'Kesselhaus' with a full PostalAddress ('Knaackstraße 97', 10435 Berlin) — the well-known real-world address of the Kulturbrauerei complex, Prenzlauer Berg. The sampled event card's own retained 'location' text is 'Kesselhaus & Maschinenhaus', and the event detail page's own JSON-LD independently restates the identical name/address.

site_classification.platform: A custom Angular Universal (server-side-rendered) application, backed by Firebase (Firebase Storage/Realtime-Database-style push IDs are directly visible in retained asset URLs, e.g. 'kessel-europe.appspot.com'). No WordPress, ICS, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal. The calendar list page's own embedded transfer-state JSON blob is the mechanism for discovering the set of upcoming event ids/URLs; each event's own detail page additionally exposes a clean, standard schema.org JSON-LD 'Event' block once that URL is known.

title.notes: The sampled event's own detail-page JSON-LD 'name' field states this directly (also independently corroborated by the calendar page's own server-rendered DOM <span class="title">). Using the JSON-LD 'name' field as the primary claim keeps this a single-piece-of-evidence DIRECT_SOURCE claim.

start_date.notes: The event's own detail-page JSON-LD 'startDate' field states a full UTC instant directly: '2026-08-01T20:00:00.000Z' (note the literal 'Z' UTC-offset suffix — an unusually precise, genuinely UTC value for this project, not merely a floating local time). The calendar page's own embedded transfer-state query result for this same event independently states the identical 'start':'2026-08-01T20:00:00.000Z', cross-confirming the value from a second, structurally distinct retained location on the same request/response set.

time.notes: The time-of-day portion of the same JSON-LD 'startDate' ('20:00:00.000Z' UTC = 22:00 local Europe/Berlin summer time, CEST/UTC+2) — a genuine UTC instant, not a floating local guess. The calendar page's own rendered local-time DOM span for the same event independently reads '10:00 PM', consistent with this UTC-to-CEST conversion.

end.notes: No end time or end date is exposed anywhere in the retained JSON-LD or transfer-state data for the sampled event.

venue_location.notes: The event's own detail-page JSON-LD 'location.name'/'location.address' fields state this directly, identical to the calendar page's own venue-level 'EventVenue' JSON-LD block.

source_record_id.notes: Each event's own Firebase-style push id, directly stated as both the transfer-state query result's own 'id' field and the literal path segment of the event's own detail-page URL ('/en/calendar/{id}'). Firebase Realtime Database push IDs are permanent, monotonically-time-ordered keys by the platform's own well-documented design (they do not regenerate on repeated fetches) — the same class of platform-native stable-identifier reasoning already accepted for razzmatazz-barcelona-01's Sanity '_id', not an inferred or merely numeric-looking value.

event_url.notes: The calendar page's own rendered <a href="/en/calendar/{id}"> for each event card, directly stated, and independently confirmed by fetching it (HTTP 200, ev-event-detail-jsonld).

price.notes: Not present in either the calendar list page or the detail page's own JSON-LD. It is present only as unstructured free text on the detail page's rendered 'Tickets' button ('VVK: 8 Euro plus Gebühren | AK: 12 Euro' — German 'Vorverkauf'/advance-sale vs. 'Abendkasse'/door price), which would need bespoke text parsing to become a structured value — genuinely not yet resolved to a precise PROVEN price.

blockers.description: Unlike moog-barcelona-01/waldbuehne-berlin-01, this source's JSON-LD 'Event' block lives only on each event's own detail page, not as one array covering every upcoming event. Discovering the current set of event ids/URLs first requires parsing the calendar page's own embedded Angular Universal transfer-state blob (a distinct EMBEDDED_JSON step, including the mechanical '&q;'->'"' unescape) before per-event JSON_LD extraction can run — a two-stage acquisition, not a one-page fetch. This project's existing generic ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs still covers the per-event extraction step unmodified; only the list-discovery step is new.
Only one real event was sampled at detail-page granularity; the transfer-state's custom escaping and per-event JSON-LD presence were not yet verified across a broader sample of events/categories.

evidence.description: Bounded excerpt of the venue's own calendar page: (1) the full retained venue-level 'EventVenue' JSON-LD block; (2) the first 6 of the real query results for the 2026-08 to 2026-09 window from the retained Angular Universal transfer-state blob, decoded by mechanically replacing every literal '&q;' with '"' and JSON-parsing (each result gives a real event id and a genuine UTC 'start' ISO timestamp); (3) the server-rendered DOM excerpt for the same event (matched by its data-id), showing its title/subtitle/local-date-parts/location/category rendered directly in HTML. Full response (1.1MB, ~1065 transfer-state keys) was fetched and inspected; this excerpt retains every region material to the field assessment above.
